utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution calls Mr. Koster to the stand, and may I introduce the Chamber to Mr. Rupert Elderkin who will examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rupert --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, Mr. Elderkin. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness, could I make one short proposal with respect to the Srebrenica trial video and that's 65 ter 26123. The proposal is the following. Because of the length of this video it's actually in four parts, and I'm concerned that unless we identify which part the particular excerpt is that's being played, that there may be confusion because each part time code starts once again at 0. If the Chamber were to look at the surrogate sheet 426123, the four ERN numbers for each part are listed and they are listed in the order that of -- of the video, so the Prosecution would submit or suggest that with respect to ERN ending 14, that that's part 1; that part 2 be the ERN ending in the number 35; part 3 the ERN ending in 16; and part 4 the ERN ending in 67. And this way whoever is using the video, if they simply say the part it, will be clear which video is being used, and Ms. Stewart will upload a different surrogate sheet to reflect this. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you at a later moment, Mr. Lukic. Have you discussed this with Mr. Lukic before?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I didn't, Your Honour. To me it seemed to be -- to make practical sense, I didn't think it would be, in light of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's purely practical, we would like to hear you. I apologise to you, Mr. Koster, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration, the text of which is handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. [In English] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Koster. Please be seated. Mr. Koster, first a preliminary question, in which language would you like to give your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to make my statement in Dutch, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it that Dutch interpreters are there. I see that there is a Dutch booth as well at this moment. Since English and French are the official languages of this Tribunal, the language -- the questions will be put either in these languages or in B/C/S; you may answer the questions in Dutch. Mr. Elderkin, are you ready to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning. Yes, I am ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Koster, you'll first be examined by Mr. Elderkin. Mr. Elderkin is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: First, could you please say your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: My first name is Eelco, my surname is Koster.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel Koster, do you recall being interviewed and providing a witness statement to the ICTY on the 25th and 26th of September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd ask please to see 65 ter 28314 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, this should be your statement coming up on the screen in front of you. I'd ask please if we could just see the Dutch first. We have three languages for this statement, so I'll show you the English and B/C/S afterwards. I don't have a screen on yet, so I need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for the Dutch version. We have it on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel Koster, is the statement in front of you on the screen the statement that you made in September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Please could we see the last page of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, looking at that final page of the statement, is that your signature on the page?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And could I also ask that we could be shown the English and B/C/S briefly for those reading in those languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Colonel Koster, have you had the opportunity to read the statement in the last few days?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I've had that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And does the statement truthfully and accurately reflect your answers during that interview?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, they accurately reflect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And do they truthfully reflect that, those answers as well?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, it's also truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Would you give the same answers and provide the same information if you were examined here today and asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember them properly, and otherwise I would refer to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request the admission of the witness's statement, 65 ter 28314, as his Rule 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Stojanovic, you're the one in charge? Oh, Mr. Petrusic, yes. I'm sorry. You changed places and -- no objections? Madam Registrar, the number would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28314 becomes Exhibit P57, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P57 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: With Your Honour's permission, I'd now like to read a short summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you explained to Mr. Koster what the purpose of this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Indeed. I'll do so again to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have then we don't have to do it again. I just wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: In 1995, Eelco Koster was a Dutch army lieutenant who served as a DutchBat's logistics officer in the Srebrenica enclave. On his arrival in January 1995, Koster was informed that there were already logistical shortages including fuel and rations. During the following months DutchBat faced fuel and food shortages. There was limited electricity, as the generators required diesel fuel, and leave requests were refused without reason. Throughout his time in Srebrenica, Koster also observed the military situation around the enclave or was informed about the situation during staff officers meetings. On the 10th of July, 1995, Koster was among some 30 DutchBat troops ordered to clear the approach route to the DutchBat compound for the fleeing Muslim population and they made a hole in the compound's perimeter fence. While waiting for the Muslims, Koster could hear firing and shells landing close by. Koster and others carried one woman into the compound who had shrapnel injuries. During the 11th to 13th of July, Koster commanded a group of DutchBat soldiers outside the compound. Koster saw the arrival of thousands of refugees, mostly women, children, and elderly men. During those days, Koster saw scenes including Serbs pushing Muslims towards buses. He saw some Muslim men sitting in a greyish-white house to the west of the road with personal belongings outside, and he saw DutchBat troops who had been disarmed. On the 12th of July, Koster saw Serb soldiers arriving in Potocari. Koster saw General Mladic arrive. Koster spoke with Mladic. He watched Mladic walking around among the refugees, which was recorded on video by the Serbs. Koster told Mladic that DutchBat commander Karremans wanted to speak to him, but Mladic said that he did not care about the UN and that he would do as he wanted and that he was now going to evacuate. When Koster protested again, Mladic was becoming annoyed and warned Koster, "If you oppose me, you will be in trouble." Later Mladic came up to Koster again and asked if he had seen any Muslim fighters or knew where they were, to which Koster said that he did not know and if he had known he would not have told him. On the 13th of July, Serb soldiers again loaded people onto buses. It was a scorching day and there was chaos with people collapsing, and everyone among the Muslim population looking out for themselves. Koster investigated a rumour about bodies lying somewhere and went to a location where there were nine bodies with gun-shot wounds in the middle of their backs. That day Koster saw Mladic driving by in a military jeep more than once. Koster heard that by about 1900 hours on the 13th of July all the refugees had been taken away. Koster left Srebrenica with DutchBat on the 21st of July and saw Mladic as the column passed the iron bridge. That concludes my summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel Koster, I now have some additional questions for you. First, please could you tell us briefly what was your current employment?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: My current employment is with the Royal Dutch Military Constabulary as deputy director of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What is your rank today?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: My rank is colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask some background questions concerning the evidence that I've just summarised and contained in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could we see, please, 65 ter 20005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What will be coming up on the screen, Colonel, is a map I'd like to look at briefly to help put in context the evidence in your statement. Here --

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If we could please zoom in towards the lower half of the map. And just zoom out slightly so we capture the town at the top of the screen right now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: So we can see Bratunac towards the top right of the screen, and then along the road running southwards Yellow Bridge, UN Dutch compound, and an arrow towards Srebrenica. Is this the area to which you were deployed in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about the location marked as "Yellow Bridge"?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Yellow Bridge is the entrance to the enclave which was a check-point we had to pass upon entering and leaving the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who held the territory to the north of the Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That was held by the Bosnian Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And to the south of the Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The Muslim population was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you explain on this map the route by which Muslims were arriving at Potocari after the July 1995 attack on the Srebrenica enclave. If you can do that just by description, that's fine; if you need to use a marker pen, please say so.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I'll describe it in words. The Muslim population arrived from the south from the direction of Srebrenica and went northward to Potocari and Bratunac. They came from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd request to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20005 becomes Exhibit P58, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P68 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Elderkin -- oh, 58, yes, I misspoke. P58 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Please could we see now 65 ter 17912.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, we can see from the printed title that this is an overview of Potocari. Do you recognise the locations here?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, may I interrupt, please. I see there are markings on this map. Were they made by this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, perhaps you could answer the question of the Judge.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, these were my own notes that I made. I also signed the notes. At the lower left, you'll see my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again, Colonel, if you can describe to us without needing to mark anything further, could you indicate where is the DutchBat compound on this image?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The compound is at the bottom centre of the photos, centre of the photo is the DutchBat compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: To clarify, would that be the largest of the buildings we can see along the left-hand side of the road as we see on the image now?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And in which direction along the road is Yellow Bridge and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yellow Bridge and Bratunac are in the direction at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And the markings we can see on the image, could you tell us in turn what they indicate. First, with the largest of the red boxes.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The marking with the largest red square indicates roughly where the refugees were located; and next you'll see a small red marking on the road, and that's the position where four armoured DutchBat vehicles were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And that would be associated with the writing "4 X APC"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that is indeed correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And there is also a line heading from the road towards the right, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That line is the route I worked with two fellow soldiers to investigate whether at the site with the bushes to the right were nine bodies, and we did indeed find them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall where a location of a bus compound or bus depot was when you look at this image?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember the bus depot was in the large red marked square.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request to tender this image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 17912 becomes Exhibit P59, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P59 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And may we see, please, 65 ter 5283.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Now, I certainly have some trouble seeing the writing on here, but this is clearly another marked image. Colonel, can you tell us whether you can actually read and see the blue lines that appear on here? If not, I'd suggest to proceed with a hard copy of the image.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I can see the blue lines easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if they're clear enough to yourselves and everyone else in the courtroom, I'd be happy to proceed with the image on the screen obviously, since that stays in the trial record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, again for orientation, we can see a road running from the top right to the centre bottom of this image. Can you tell us along that road which direction is Yellow Bridge and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Along this road, Yellow Bridge and Bratunac would be at the top end of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask you about the markings we can see on here, starting with the circle towards the top, centre right, and that has the words "white house" next to it. What is that location?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That location, as far as I can remember, is the white house where the Muslim men were gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: When you say where the Muslim men were gathered, who were these Muslim men and over what period were they gathered there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: These Muslim men were the men taken from among the refugees, and that happened around the 12th and 13th of July, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, before we proceed, I noticed that what you are at this moment show to the witness is, as a matter of fact, a picture which has been rotated, apparently by the usher, and that could lead to confusion if we are talking about the top of the map or east or -- so therefore I suggest that we look at the picture as it was uploaded into e-court, and then we would have to understand, I think, the first answer of the witness to be that Yellow Bridge and Bratunac would be to the right of the map -- of the picture rather than to the top. Mr. Koster, could you please look at it because if we start rotating images then your testimony does not -- is not valid anymore. Could you confirm that as shown now that Yellow Bridge and Bratunac is to the right end of the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I think the reference to the white house is clear enough since the wording appears next to that marking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: -- unless you would like me to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that is now at the right edge of this picture. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, could you tell us where the white house appears on this image in relation to the DutchBat compound, the one that we saw in the previous aerial image?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The white house is located -- well, let me put it differently. The compound is at the lower right of the photograph with respect to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And there's a marking along the road where I see reference to APCs, that's towards the left-hand edge of the screen as we see it along the road. Could you tell us what that marking indicates?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. That's the position at which the four APCs are positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: When were those APCs in position at that location?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: They were positioned there on July 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who positioned them there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The APCs were positioned there at my request and the drivers positioned them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Why did you decide to position APCs at that location?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I decided to position the APCs there to facilitate security for the Muslim population and to streamline it. I positioned the APCs there as a type of barrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Now, we can see some arrows going diagonally from close to the APC marking towards the top right of the image. Please can you tell us what do they represent?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The arrows mark the route I walked with two fellow soldiers to the location where we suspected that nine bodies would be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And indeed there is a marking, a line, and the word "bodies" up towards the top right in the uniform green area. Can you please tell us again what that marking specifically indicates.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's the position where we found nine bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And close to that marking there is a cross in a circle and the letter E. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That marks the spot where we left the road and entered the meadow where the nine bodies were found, and the E means that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again, close to that letter E there is a line pointing towards an X and the words "Serb soldier." Can you tell us what that represents?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. When we left the meadow to report, we were found by a Bosnian Serb soldier at roughly that position and then started speaking on his radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And there's also nearby an arrow that does a loop back on itself and that's along what appears to be a roadway or a path heading horizontally towards the right top hand of the screen. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That line marks the route we selected after the Bosnian Serb soldier saw us. We then assumed that this soldier, because he was speaking into a radio, was reporting and that's why we used a different route to return to the compound. When we walked onto that route we were shot at and we returned, and then we walked back along the route marked by arrows and went to the compound passed the APCs. Eventually I stopped at the APCs and took on my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd like to leave this image on the screen while I briefly cover some additional detail about the nine bodies that you describe in your statement. Can you tell us what you saw when you arrived at these bodies; for example, were they grouped together or spread apart? As best you recall, what was the scene that you saw?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: When we arrived there we saw nine bodies lying on their stomachs and they were roughly in a line. The bodies had gun-shot wounds around the middle of the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were the bodies all in the same orientation, the heads at the same end, or mixed in both directions?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the bodies were roughly all in the same orientation and also roughly in a row, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again, apart from what you say in your statement, can you recall any additional detail about how you assessed the bodies, specifically any indication that you observed about how long ago they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I remember once again that the bodies were on their stomachs and were primarily dressed in men's clothes, I mean that they were wearing trousers, and the bodies had gun-shot wounds around the middle of the back and those injuries seemed recent to me because the blood hadn't crusted yet. So it seemed like the bodies had laid there for at most a half day or a few hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall any smell?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No. I didn't smell any strange smell there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were there any weapons nearby or any other indication that these men could have been soldiers and not civilians?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I did not find any weapons there in those surroundings. There were various documents on the ground, and as far as I can remember these men, or at least their bodies, were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5283 becomes Exhibit P60, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P60 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: May we please see 65 ter 4820.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: The title here indicates the image shows Potocari on the 12th of July of 1995 at around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, you'll see there are some indications on here added to the aerial image itself, including two large arrows. These are not relevant to this witness. This is simply the image that we have in e-court as it is, and I'd ask, with your permission, that we could proceed. I'll ask the witness simply about the image, not about those additions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. You may proceed as suggested. By the way, here you say you have given it a date. Two images back there was a date on it as well, but that was the 13th of July apparently that -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, again to orientate the Court to this image, can you see any part of the DutchBat compound --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Could I invite both the accused and Defence counsel, if they want to communicate, to do it at such a level of voice that it doesn't disturb the Chamber in hearing the evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, to orientate us, can you see any part of the DutchBat compound in this picture?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The DutchBat compound is at the lower right of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And again, which direction on this image is Bratunac and Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yellow Bridge and Bratunac are also situated at the lower right of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you see the bus depot here?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The bus depot is at the centre and bottom left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Now, can you please look along the road in the image. Do you recall the general scene on that road when you were in Potocari on the afternoon of 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the road proceeding to the top left, it's the road along which the refugees came in the direction of Potocari, that's that road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And where the indication in the centre of the image says "People," can you tell us what you see on the road and particularly what you recall seeing on that day in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That is the location where we sent the -- our red-and-white band to mark the point up to where the civilian population could proceed further on safety, and as far as I can see there are indeed a lot of refugees around that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Where were you personally positioned during the course of that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I was in various positions around the bus depot in the centre of the photograph, but most of the time I was at the spot where I indicated the red-and-white band was, where you see the "People" marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And according to your statement, you had several encounters with General Mladic on the 12th of July. Do you recall where those encounters took place?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. That's at the position indicated and marked as "People" and it was on the road, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request to tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- oh, Mr. Petrusic, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence does not object to the admission of this document, but we wish to know who it was that introduced changes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot here the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- the interpreters were unable to hear the last part of what you said. You asked who made the changes and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. That was my question, this intervention, who introduced these changes as far as the photographs are concerned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the markings "People," "Trucks," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether I have to ask this to Mr. Koster or -- Mr. Koster, if you know who made -- put the text into this, if you know, please tell us; otherwise, we'll ask Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no idea, Your Honour. In any case, I didn't position them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the image was provided to us from a Rule 70 provider with all of the text in -- the black text in the white boxes is how we received the images. I understand, but I would have to confirm if it's a point of contention, that the two arrows on the image were added by one of the OTP investigators for purposes of presentation. But as I said in the beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said the Prosecution will not rely on the red arrows. We have not heard what they mean. You received the document in this format?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Exactly -- as we have seen with the preceding aerial image as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Petrusic, I also heard you say that there's no objection against admission. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4820 becomes Exhibit P61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P61 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I may proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: May we see, please, 65 ter 6189. This is similar to the last image and again the title indicates that the image shows Potocari, this time on the 13th of July, 1995, again at around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again for orientation, Colonel, can you please tell us if you can identify the DutchBat compound on this image?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The DutchBat compound is situated at the bottom left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again, looking along the road that we see in the image, does the general scene portrayed here from the air correspond with what you observed when you were present in Potocari on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I could see from my position, yes, it does correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were there people present along the road on the 13th July 1995, any crowds of people or groups of people, that you observed when you were there?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I saw a great many Muslim refugees along the road, and from the barrier we set up with the four APCs they were proceeding to the buses, and I also saw Bosnian Serb soldiers along the road as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you identify the location of the barrier on the road on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, the barrier is located along the road at the upper end where the vehicles on the road are located, and perhaps it might be convenient if I indicated them with a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: That would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I could ask for the court usher's assistance. Can I ask that we have the markings set up in a red pen so that they are distinct for this trial. Hopefully it may avoid some confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general, any markings made at the request of the Prosecution will be marked in red, whereas any marking made at the request of the Defence will be made in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, if I could ask you using the pen to first mark a line where, as best you recall, there was a barrier across the road.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The barrier was about there and that was the barrier with the APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And that's the horizontal line you've drawn across the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And if we could continue with the pen and ask for a further marking which would be to identify if he can say where was the crowd of people that you observed. Can you place a circle around the general area.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's the area where I saw the people, both behind the barrier and around the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And those are the only markings I'd ask from the witness for this image. I'd ask if we could have that admitted as a marked in-court exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6189 marked by the witness becomes Exhibit P62, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P62 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, was the barrier across the road in the same position on the 13th of July as on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I issued instructions on the morning of July 13th to take up positions with the APCs there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit. I'd now like to start using some short sections of the trial compilation video of Srebrenica. They're very short --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, sorry for interrupting you. The last question was not properly answered. You asked if the barrier was at the same position as the day before; this is not answered. You should ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, perhaps you could explain if the barrier was indeed in the same position when you put it up on the 13th of July or was it in a different position, as compared with the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, on July 12th I didn't have such a barrier involving vehicles set up, I had that done on July 13th. So on July 12th, as far as I can remember, these vehicles were not yet in this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And the location of the red-and-white tape across the road in the 12th compared to the position of the vehicles in the 13th, were those the same positions or was the tape at a different location?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: The red-and-white tape was at a different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And was that closer towards the DutchBat compound compared to the vehicles, as we see on the 13th, or further away from the DutchBat compound?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No. The red-and-white tape was further away from the compound and roughly at the top of the circle marking I placed on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I see we have perhaps five minutes left before the first scheduled break and the first video clip I would play is less than a minute long, so I'll proceed until we run out of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd like to see from 65 ter 26123 and from part 1 of the compilation, which is ERN V0009014, a video starting at 14 minutes, 59 seconds, through to 15 minutes, 31 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recall scenes like this as we've just seen on that sequence of video?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Such trucks completely loaded with refugees and wounded refugees did pass my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Where was your position around that time on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: At the time my position was outside the compound in the area of the former bus station, and these vehicles rode passed this bus station to reach the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Where were these people coming from?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: These people came from the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: The next clip is from part 2 of the compilation and it's -- that's V0009035 from 17 minutes, 57 seconds, through to 19 minutes, 7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can play it, but then we have no further time for questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, unless it would be one very short question, but if there are more questions then we will -- they can be put to the witness after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: They can all wait until after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you already follow the usher who will escort you out of the courtroom. We will take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, are you on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'll finish within the 90 minutes total that we indicated for this witness, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we take a break and we resume at 20 minutes passed 10.00, and could I invite everyone to be ready at 20 minutes passed 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, we finished just before the break with that short section of video, showing scene around soldiers, crowd, some UN blue helmets in Potocari. Were you in the area we saw in the video on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you see these kinds of scenes?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I saw these scenes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could we please see from 19 minutes, 47 [Realtime transcript read in error, "57"] seconds, and pausing at 19 minutes, 55 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, as it reads on the transcript you are moving backwards in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And it should read, Your Honour, 19 minutes, 47 seconds to 19.55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you for observing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And we're paused at 19 minutes, 55.1 according to the counter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you identify the man in the blue helmet who has just walked on to the centre of the screen?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I'm that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could we please see from exactly 24 minutes and then pause at 24 minutes, 23 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And we have paused at 24 minutes, 23.8 seconds according to the counter on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, can you identify the people on the screen, starting from the blue helmet on the left?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The person wearing the blue helmet at the left of the photograph is me, then the second person wearing a blue helmet is the United Nations military observer, the UNMO. The gentleman -- I don't recognise the gentleman in the centre wearing glasses, and the man at the right of the photograph, I know him as Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall what is going on here?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the moments that I'm talking to Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could we carry on playing, please, through to 24 minutes and 50 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, did you remain in the area while General Mladic was talking to Muslims in the crowd at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remained at that location. I was not consistently close to Mladic's position. Sometimes I reported about the position of DutchBat and I tried to converse with Mladic at multiple occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What did you see General Mladic doing while you saw him around the Muslims in Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I saw him talking to the Muslims. I saw him soothing children by touching them and patting them, and I saw him doing things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who was with General Mladic when you saw him around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: There were -- there is Bosnian Serb soldiers around Mladic, including one or two body-guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you see the video cameraman who would have made this footage or any other footage from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I did indeed see camera people recording videos there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall that they were dressed as civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I apologise, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic speak to any of the Bosnian Serb soldiers around him?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: At the moment that I'm talking with General Mladic, I did see him talking in the direction of Bosnian Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And just a reference to the previous aerial images we were looking at, does the location we've seen in this sequence of video correspond with the aerial image we saw of Potocari taken at around 1400 hours on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, yes, that was in the area of the red-and-white tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could we please now see part 3 of the compilation video, which is ERN V0009016, and that's starting first extract at 2 minutes, 43 seconds, through to 3 minutes, 30 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recall seeing these kinds of scenes when you were out on the road in Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I saw such scenes of Muslims at several points, Muslims being directed to the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can we see, please, from 5 minutes, 42 seconds, pausing at 5 minutes, 46 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, did you see any instances of men being separated from the rest of the crowd during either the 12th or the 13th of July in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I did indeed see that, and where we were able to prevent it we tried get the Muslim men back in the flow of refugees, and I did so myself as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you recall any specific detail about your own attempts to try to prevent separations?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, at a certain point I respond to yelling by a young man, who was being removed from the flow of refugees by two or three Bosnian Serb soldiers. His mother was there and was protesting, and I went there and tried to get the boy back into the flow of refugees. Together with his mother at first I didn't succeed, but I continued urging and based on my rank they let the boy go, they released him, and I was able to direct him back into the flow of refugees so that he was able to board the buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: How old did he seem to be to you, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I think that young man would have been about 15 or 16 years old, around that age.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you or any of the DutchBat soldiers under your command take part in the process of separating men from the crowd?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No, we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who was doing the separations?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see, the men were separated from the refugees by Bosnian Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Please could we see from 6 minutes and 8 seconds, pausing at 6 minutes and 16 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: We're paused at 6 minutes, 16.4 seconds according to the counter on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is the man in the middle wearing the blue flak jacket?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, the man wearing the blue flak jacket, I recognise him as Mickey, who together with the man at the left of the screen was basically in command on site. They issued all kinds of instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Which organisation do you understand this man to be part of? Was he DutchBat? Bosnian Muslim? Bosnian Serb?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No, the man wearing the blue flak jacket in the centre of the photograph was part of the Bosnian Serb soldiers, as far as I'm concerned [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And the man in the beret on the right of the screen, who is he?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I recognise him as a fellow soldier, van Duijn of DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can we please carry on to 6 minutes, 31, and pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And we're paused at 6 minutes, 31.3 seconds according to the counter on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: This is to give us a clearer view of the man you mentioned to be known to you as Mane. You confirm now seeing him face on the screen that is the man you recall as Mane?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I do, indeed, recognise that man as being named Mane.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And to be clear, again, which organisation was he part of?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: He pertained to the Bosnian Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Final clip I'd like to show you, please, is from 10 minutes, 21 seconds, through to 10 minutes, 54 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I recognise this location as the location I designated as the white house where the Muslim men from the population were gathered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you see this location personally during the 12th or 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I was there on one of the days, not at the actual house but I was nearby. And at the time I saw men sitting on the ground against the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. And in your statement you referred to seeing Mladic in Potocari on the 13th of July. Can you tell us how you saw him, where you saw him, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I saw Mladic riding passed there in a car from the direction of Potocari to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I've finished my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Fluegge would like to put a short question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In relation to the white house, you told us that you have been nearby the white house. Have you any idea how many people were gathered in this white house at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing I can tell you, Your Honour, is that when I was nearby that white house I saw about ten men sitting at the house at the time. I have no indication how many people, how many men, were being detained at the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, are you ready to start your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Petrusic is a member of the Mladic Defence team. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, my first question is this: You arrived in Srebrenica on the 21st of January, 1995, or rather, in Potocari. Which rank did you have in the Dutch Battalion at the time?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: At the time my rank was 1st Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What was your duty in the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: My duty when I arrived in the enclave was that of a logistics lieutenant, that was my function.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were involved in providing supplies, materiel, and all other necessities required by the battalion in order for it to be operational during the mission?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I did indeed work for the logistics section that was involved in supply of logistics and convoys of people on leave for the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: By reading your statement and listening to your evidence, my conclusion is that on a number of occasions you went on patrol duty inside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 1D00093 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise it -- I withdraw this question. The handwriting that you can see, can you acknowledge that this is your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I can confirm that that's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If I understand it correctly, this is a questionnaire given to you by the ICTY in order to give answers to the questions already asked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 4 in English and page 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this handwriting that you see in the upper and right-hand portions of this page, is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that as my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning you were asked whether you had personally witnessed inhumane and brutal treatment -- I withdraw this question. Let me ask you this: Does this questionnaire relate to the Srebrenica event that took place in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, isn't that very obvious? There's no need to ask about matters which are obvious anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So, Colonel, on page 6 you can see that you provided answers by encircling either a yes or no in response to the questions. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Under item 5 it says: "Wanton destruction or theft of private property ..." And you encircled: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not ask a question to the witness? I mean, it's -- everyone can read that there's "yes" after this question. So please develop so that we hear evidence which is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you whether there was only wanton destruction in Srebrenica, what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: Whether I saw whether there was wanton destruction or theft, is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you if I put a question to you that there was only wanton destruction, which you of course should have seen, what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is totally unclear to me. Mr. Petrusic, I do not know what you are seeking. We see that the witness filled in on this form at the question that he observed wanton destruction or theft of private property, he said "yes." Now please put a clear question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put the following question, whether he had seen only wanton destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "only" in this respect? Whether there was destruction which was not wanton or - that's not clear to me - or whether he didn't see anything else. He may have seen vehicles, he may have seen people. What do you mean by "only"? Or is your question whether he saw any destruction which could not be considered to be wanton destruction of private property; is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My question is whether he saw destruction that could be considered wanton. Obviously this is an interpretation problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then rephrase the question in such a way that everyone is able to understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you in Srebrenica, did you see wanton destruction of the town?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: In the period that I was in the enclave, I was in the city of Srebrenica on some occasions and I saw the destruction of houses and the destruction of various locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was that after the 11th of July, or rather, after the 6th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That was both before the 6th of July and after the 6th of July and around the 11th of July, and in the final period I was primarily in the area of Potocari and the reception area for the refugees. Before that, I rode through Srebrenica and the enclave several times and patrolled there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, the word "destruction" may be not always unambiguous. When you say "I saw destruction," did you mean that you saw features that were destroyed or did you see the destruction going on? I mean, if you see a house hit by a shell which may have hit a house a couple of days before, then you see the destruction; but you do not see the shell hitting the house and -- or destruction. When you use the word "destruction," what do you mean? Destruction ongoing at that very moment or the traces or the results of what -- the result being destruction of a house or a feature or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, both cases are true. In the period before July 11th I saw houses that had already been destroyed, so I didn't see the process of destruction. In the period around July 11th and afterwards, I also saw -- I also saw shells landing and machine-gun fire between the houses and destroying them. I saw that process at the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, just one more question as regards this topic. Which houses were in Potocari had been destroyed? Maybe my concept of destruction does not coincide with yours, but you're an officer, you're a soldier, and I think that you know what the real meaning of that concept is. So which buildings in Potocari were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know whether we interpret the concepts the same way, but what I saw is that around my position at around July 11th shells hit the houses that were around my position, I saw that. And I'm describing that as destructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said towards the end of January Muslim fighters wanted you to stay away from part of the enclave. Can you tell us which part of the enclave that was and why it was that they had asked you to do that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I recall, that would have been the section described as the Bandera Triangle. In that period we - in this case UNPROFOR, not me personally - were denied access to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many UNPROFOR soldiers and officers were taken prisoner on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I recall that happened in stages, and in the end about 70 to 100 UNPROFOR soldiers were detained there. That's what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What about Major Boering who went to negotiate after the first prisoners were taken? Was he also arrested by the same group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, I read: "When this happened, Major Boering and van Alphen went to negotiate and were also taken hostage by the BiH [indiscernible]." So therefore that question seems to be answered in the statement. Could you please focus on whatever we need in addition to the statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I just wanted to lay that by way of a foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So did your command protest? Did it lodge a protest with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo, or rather, did you protest with the appropriate command of UNPROFOR north-east, in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So, quite simply, you never went to that zone again?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I don't know to what extent you can associate that, but I can't recall that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you ever try to disarm that part of the zone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: It's not a direct objection, but the reference to "you," as it comes across in English, is at least leading me to read references to the witness personally, and it seems that the questions are directed at DutchBat generally, and it may help for the record for that to be specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Petrusic, that you are not only talking about the witness but also about other members of DutchBat. Then the question was whether you ever tried - you or DutchBat people - tried to disarm that part of the zone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Further on you say that in the spring of 1995 you noticed troop movements from Zvornik. These troops from Zvornik in the spring, that is to say the time that you are speaking about, did they arrive in the area of Srebrenica or did they carry out any kind of combat activity in the area of Srebrenica? So we're talking about the early spring of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, it would assist the Chamber if you would guide us to the relevant page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just a moment. It is page 4 in English and page 3 in Serbian -- oh, no, no, no. I've made a mistake. All right, Mr. President, I'll go back to that later and now I shall move on. What I quoted just now is on page 4 -- just a minute. Page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I think Mr. Petrusic appears to refer to the first paragraph, page 4, line 4 and 5: "I also heard that there had been troop movements in Zvornik ..." If that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we had found it meanwhile, but thank you anyhow. Mr. Petrusic, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So these troops, did they arrive in the protected area?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, they were not in the protected area in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So on the same page, page 4, in the English version it is paragraph 4 and in the Serbian version it is page 3, you say that food was running out. So you did not have enough food. Did I understand you correctly, in that period you did not have enough food?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: In that period we had food but we had to ration it. The normal food -- the food supply was below what we would normally have had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D0073 is the number of the document that I'd like to have displayed now. Before I speak about this document, Mr. President, I shall tender this statement which had been put, or rather, this questionnaire, 1D00093, that is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D00093 becomes Exhibit D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D25 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Petrusic, as general guidance, if you want to put a document to the witness about things that were documented, better first ask the witness whether he has any knowledge about it. That it's more appropriate to find that out before a document is put to the witness than after putting to the witness a document and then to hear from him that he doesn't know anything about what's described in that document. Could you please keep that in the back of your mind and you may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, were you aware of the situation in which your command approved and provided supplies, that is to say both food and fuel, to members of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So if I were to put a document to you, the one that's on the screen, 1D00073, would that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please, if I were to read the last paragraph out to you: "We note that the above mentioned quantities have been separated out of the humanitarian aid contingent which arrived in the area through UNHCR while some of the food was obtained from the Dutch Battalion." Who would be the person from the Dutch Battalion who could approve these supplies?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: That's difficult. I don't remember the situation properly or don't remember it at all in fact, and in any case I don't recognise this letter so that makes it difficult for me to indicate who would have approved that and I'd like to leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: A question of principle. I'm not saying that you approved it, but the question of principle, supplies, logistics supplies, would you be the person to approve that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO KOSTER
utterances.text: No. Ultimately it was the battalion's head of logistics, and I was his deputy -- excuse me, I was his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, perhaps I put one additional question. Do you have any knowledge or are you aware of ever DutchBat providing food to the defence -- the Muslim defence or the 28th I think it was Battalion. But are you aware of ever having provided food to the military, the Muslim military, in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you don't remember or you remember that it did never happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrusic, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we are close to a break and I have a few procedural matters I would like to deal with, therefore I suggest that Mr. Koster takes the break already and that we briefly deal with these procedural matters. For you it would be approximately half an hour that we would like to see you back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matters I would like to deal with, first about scheduling post the summer recess. On the 16th of July, the Chamber indicated to the parties a possible schedule for the period between the summer and winter recess of this year. On the 17th of July, 2012, the Defence made its submissions on this matter. It stated that it did not object to the weeks of adjournment identified by the Chamber, but proposed that the number of sitting days per week be reduced to four. Further, the Defence proposed that the daily start time should be moved from 9.00 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. and that the Chamber sit for shorter sessions between breaks. The Prosecution indicated that it would not make any submission on this matter. The Chamber notes that neither party objects to the weeks of adjournment proposed by the Chamber. The Chamber therefore schedules hearings in this case for all weeks between the summer and winter recess with the exception of the weeks of the 13th of August, the 10th of September, the 15th and the 22nd of October, and the 26th of November. With regard to the proposed reduction from five to four court days per week for reasons related to the health of the accused, the Chamber considers that this is a measure affecting the overall scheduling of the case, and therefore requires specific submissions by the parties, accompanied by supporting medical documentation. Absent such submissions and documentation, the Chamber at this stage denies the request. The Chamber grants in part the remaining request by the Defence. On the 21st, the 22nd, and 23rd of August, the hearing will start at 9.00 a.m.; however, as from the 24th of August, the hearing will start at 9.30 a.m. The daily court sessions will be divided into three one-hour sessions and one session of 45 minutes, with always 20-minute breaks. The daily court sessions therefore will conclude at 2.15 p.m. I have a few other matters. One of them is that Mr. Groome made a proposal in relation to adjudicated facts. He made this proposal in court on the 18th of July, and the Chamber would like to know whether the Defence wishes to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that we haven't consulted fully on this with the Prosecution, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait and we'll further hear from you. The procedure with regard to agreed facts, Mr. Groome also made a proposal on the 18th of July, and the Chamber wondered whether the Defence has already made up its mind on this matter or whether there's still conversations ongoing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not only are the conversations still ongoing, but we will probably decide what can we offer to the Prosecution as we read more and more documents and witness statements in the future. So I think it will be ongoing process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the proposal was not on the subject but rather on the procedure. Would you disagree with the procedure as proposed by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber will consider whether or not to grant it, now knowing the position of the Defence. Mr. Groome, you also would like to make a proposal with regard to 65 ter numbers. How much time would that take?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the present practice that the Prosecution is following concerns the following situation. A number of the statements that the Prosecution will be tendering in this case were specifically drafted for another case and they refer to 65 ter numbers assigned to exhibits in that other case. Obviously, these exhibits have different numbers in this case. The Prosecution has done with the witnesses to date and proposes to continue to do is to attach to the back of the statement a conversion chart that correlates the 65 ter number mentioned in the statement with the 65 ter number assigned in this case. The Prosecution proposes to actually attach it to the statement to ensure it never becomes separated from the statement and thereby causing confusion. Now, in discussions with the Legal Officer of the Chamber and Mr. Lukic, there are some other concerns with respect to possible confusion later in the trial, and we are actively exploring technical solutions for that, but I would propose for the time being that we -- Prosecution be allowed to maintain this practice of attaching a conversion chart to the back of any exhibit that so requires it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Groome, of course for today the system will not change, but of course the Chamber would very much like the parties to seek a joint resolution as soon as possible. And, Mr. Lukic, if you have already --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- anything to add to this, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- sentence, Your Honour. I think that -- this is, I think, the only system the Prosecution can utilise at this moment, but at the end of this trial we will have complete chaos. It will be impossible for everybody, Chambers, Prosecution, us to follow. After two, three years, who would remember what happened with which witness and which number was assigned to the wrong document. So if we search, we would find the document but that document would be different in our case, so I don't know -- we have -- we have to find a solution, but this is maybe some kind of semi-solution but it's not a proper one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, for today we're not going to change it, but I also urge that a solution to be found as quickly as possible. Of course Chambers staff will assist the parties to the extent possible, but I see the problems when in the documents themselves we're still working with the old 65 ter numbers. At least it's now clearly on the record that this problem should be resolved as quickly as possible and we now first take a break and we resume at ten minutes to 12.00. I'll then first read a short -- no, no, I'm -- I apologise. No, 20 minutes to 12.00. I'll then first read a short decision and then we'll complete the cross-examination of Mr. Koster. Mr. Petrusic, could you give us any indication as to how much time you'd still need with Mr. Koster?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hopefully I shall finish by the end of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber encourages you to be well organised in the conduct of your cross-examination. We take a break and we'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, would you please not speak loudly when the Chamber wants to proceed. You always can consult with counsel, but please at a low volume if there's any need to do it during the sessions. I'll start reading a decision and perhaps meanwhile the witness could be -- remain stand-by, although the decision is quite a number of pages. The Chamber will now deliver its decision on the urgent Defence motion seeking adjournment and continuance of trial or, in the alternative, a reconsideration of the statement amending the guidance on the tendering of evidence through Rule 92 ter of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, filed on the 9th of July, 2012. On the 19th of June, the Chamber provided the parties with a courtesy party of its additional clarification and amendment on the guidance on the tendering and presentation of evidence, which was subsequently on the 9th of July formally put on the record. Also on this 9th of July, 2012, the Defence filed a motion requesting that the Chamber grant a six-month adjournment of the proceedings or, in the alternative, that it reconsider its additional clarification and amendment to the guidance. On the 10th of July, the Prosecution responded in court and both parties then made further oral submissions. The Defence submits that since the announcement of the guidance in November 2011, it had organised all its preparations for the trial in accordance with the relevant guide-lines therein, for which the Chamber had repeatedly stressed its preference. It argues that this drastic and unprecedented last-minute change threatens the integrity of the proceedings and the accused's right to a fair trial.
